## The most important findings for the next owner-directed work

1. **The live board representation has a concrete unresolved identity problem.**
   Hero Ice Wizard's raw public ID203000023 was originally omitted. A first alias
   repaired the omission, then native-name evidence showed that the same ID also
   describes FloatingCube and IceCube auxiliary objects. The active canonical
   path can therefore treat auxiliary objects as ordinary Hero bodies. The later
   isolated named-character reader/adapter keeps exact Hero bodies and excludes
   those full-body aliases, with independently checked original bytes and a
   bounded current-client passive check. It has not been activated in the owner's
   worker. IceCube mechanics remain unqualified. Evolved Elite Barbarians13000043
   has proved identity and a qualified isolated overlay, also unactivated.
   The existing owner-authorized Hero ability heuristic reads the original raw
   frame separately; the isolated model-input adapter does not normalize that
   path. Same-ID object selection and ability-cost effects still need review.
2. **The observed overdefense has not been reduced to one proved cause.** The
   tower session showed 288 confirmed cards costing 806 elixir, plus 16 ability
   receipts whose costs were excluded. It included 48 Logs, 24 Tornadoes and
   3 Rockets. No CPU starvation or forced-spend event was established. Two
   apparently empty-board Logs had incoming Barrels. Existing friendly defenders,
   projectiles, abilities, later counter availability and both-lane damage must
   remain visible when grading whether an additional defense was justified.
3. **Public hand reconstruction is useful information with incomplete coverage.**
   The Mirror-aware development reader achieved 4,253/4,367 exact full estimates
   over 10,424 queries: 97.39% conditional precision, 41.89% coverage. Direct memory
   identities do not guarantee that the public observer sees every play at its
   original time; sightings can be missed, delayed or merged. The matched hand
   learning trial failed its continuation filters. The flag stays off, and its
   rejected weights cannot become a continuation parent.
4. **Broader imitation learning still fits PLAY and placement weakly.** Longer
   training and dropout removal failed their material Rocket and protection
   requirements. A small quarantined dropout-free fit succeeded on its own
   balanced training assay, but that success did not carry over to the broad
   training set. Exact-input contradictions were measured and cannot explain the
   broad Rocket weakness. Gradient, label-lattice and decomposition diagnostics
   narrow specific explanations without establishing one overall learning cause.
5. **Aggregate agreement conceals meaningful action tradeoffs.** Several apparent
   overall improvements came from more correct WAIT predictions while correct
   PLAY declined. The hand trial and outcome RL examples are decomposed below.
   Existing acceptance scores did not measure the cost of unnecessary defense or
   the value of retaining a counter through the next attack. Full reactive
   sequences are still needed for that question.
6. **Outcome RL variants did not deliver the required tactical gains.** Lambda1,
   larger full/late curricula, and related controlled variants all failed their
   frozen continuation requirements. The credit audit measured long terminal
   lags; the gradient audit did not show critic gradient domination. Preserve
   these distinct results and every failed execution/recovery receipt.
7. **The source and physical-evidence limits remain consequential.** Existing
   untouched exact-Icebow confirmation has no opposing Barrel source decks and
   limited spawner opportunities. All 183 reserved exact-Icebow groups stay
   reserved. Updated simulator mechanics and isolated impact fixtures improved
   the instruments, while current-client tactical parity and complete safe-cycle
   resource attribution remain unresolved.

Prepared October 6, 2026, as a documentation-only transition component. Read the newest [HANDOFF](HANDOFF.md) and the main Claude transition record for the final process, STOP, replay-completion and publication state. This file does not authorize or register an experiment.

The owner's latest direction is to finish the current turn and stop so Claude can take over. The existing worker heartbeat was paused by the parent agent. Earlier overnight cutoffs were superseded by owner-supervised continuation; that continuation is now bounded by this new stop request. Preserve the owner's live worker and its sources. No new experiment, passive collection, training, live restart, source integration or flag activation follows from this registry.

## 1. Owner objectives that remain unmet

The owner wants a NEW model materially and statistically better than R1e across the full requested behavior set, with sustained trophy progress beyond 11,000. A win in one aggregate metric cannot close the objective while another required component fails.

Those logs alone cannot grade each spell's value. Two zero-enemy-body Log examples had incoming Barrels. |

## 2. Quantified mandatory final replacement floors

The governing source is [master PLAN: Strong replacement acceptance](scratchpad/gauntlet/L72/improvement_loop/PLAN.md). Preserve all applicable controls and component requirements. These thresholds were declared before successor training and cannot be lowered to promote a failed candidate.

| Final measure | Required floor | Required design / unresolved details |

| Reactive wins | At least **+8 pp** over fresh R1e; paired **95% CI lower bound > 0**; **at least 192 predeclared matched games**; **no opponent-family regression** | Freeze scenarios, seeds, family membership and complete outcomes. Any expansion uses a declared power rule before results. The minimum is a floor; adequacy still requires a power assessment. |

| Barrel correct gated lane responses | **At least +15 pp** on **at least 100 unambiguous independent opportunities** | Validate public flight-to-landing interpretation separately. Missing coverage remains an explicit blocker. |

Use replay/match-clustered paired uncertainty, exact denominators, independent groups and complete failures. Rows, mirrored views, draws and repeated windows from one replay are correlated. Freeze final cohort membership, event definitions, controls, exclusions, sufficient sample sizes/power, selection rules and the treatment of multiple confirmation metrics before final policy evaluation. The master plan requires multiplicity handling but does not yet specify a universal Holm/Bonferroni rule or a completed final power calculation; that design remains open.

All relevant metrics/control comparisons must pass together. PLAY/WAIT decomposition is mandatory whenever an aggregate can improve by changing WAIT alone. Report gate/card/aim and the full action separately, with every replay's counts. Preserve exact original continuous **distance <= 1 tile** where that agreement criterion is registered; values slightly above one remain misses. ## 4. Physical and public-state definitions

At equal crowns, the owner's damage lead is:

**minimum raw HP of own standing crown towers minus minimum raw HP of enemy standing crown towers.**

Retain crowns, king/princess identity, raw HP/max-HP provenance, alive/standing/known flags and both lanes. Destroyed towers are accounted through crowns; unknowns stay unknown. Summed or normalized HP and princess-only margins may be reported as separately named descriptors.

Separate overtime from actual elixir multiplier. The existing model sees elapsed time, double-elixir and overtime, plus public tower/history/cycle information. No explicit triple flag or persistent per-X-Bow outcome summary was found in the earlier inspection. The historical adaptation source lacked explicit multiplier, causal-hit and entity-target records; clock bins cannot establish measured triple-elixir or lock success.

Complete sequence accounting includes initial X-Bow, all supports, Rockets, Tornado and abilities; accepted and refused/unconfirmed actions; remaining elixir; card return time; subsequent enemy pressure; both-lane tower damage/crowns; lead retention; and final outcome/tiebreak. Preserve original fixed 10/30/60-second windows and incomplete/truncated cases where used; a shortened window cannot be called complete. Six elixir at one instant does not establish a safe 12/18-elixir sequence.

Keep geometry, target intent, actual lock, causal damage and observed concurrent HP change separate in the data. Missing shooter/target provenance leaves attribution unknown. Public bodies, projectiles, effects and friendly defenders all matter; air/ground mismatch, lane, HP and multiple threats provide legitimate extra-spending controls. Card count, body count, low expenditure or a lower play probability alone cannot establish better defense.

No hidden opponent hand/deck/next/elixir or private readiness enters the policy. Future events may serve only a registered offline target/audit purpose and must never leak into causal public inputs. Original expert action/aim labels stay intact. No hand-written Rocket/Log/anti-leak/X-Bow/counter-retention rules, forced six-elixir savings or reward for spell/holding frequency. Owner observations and bot decisions remain diagnosis sources.

Simulator instruments retain their native-client parity limitations. Preserve updated RoyaleSim/RoyaleGym and native source/runtime fingerprints, actual accepted commands, complete final states and public-input audits. Applicable updated-runtime validation reached 1,603 Rust passes, zero assertion failures and three ignored timings; optional examples/skips/private-capture limitations remain and completed validation must not be repeated without a new relevant reason.

## 5. Additional ladder requirement: prospective numbers still open

The [recovery plan, section D](scratchpad/gauntlet/L72/improvement_loop/DEFENSE_AND_LADDER_RECOVERY_20261006.md) requires sustained positive trophy progress beyond 11,000 over repeated sessions and a demonstrated advantage over R1e. ## 7. Hand reader, Mirror and retention boundaries

The [original reader review](scratchpad/gauntlet/L72/improvement_loop/opponent_hand_reader/REVIEW.md) and current HANDOFF retain both ideal accepted-event and observed-public-event results. Exact object identity supplied by memory does not guarantee complete, correctly ordered play sightings: PublicObserver can miss, merge or delay events, and same-tick ambiguity persists.

- Original reader public development full-hand estimates: **4,245/4,354 correct**, **97.50% conditional precision**, **41.77% coverage** across 10,424 queries.
- Mirror-aware successor: **4,253/4,367 correct**, **97.39% conditional precision**, **41.89% coverage**. Mirror inference added eight correct and five wrong full estimates. Conditional precision must always be accompanied by coverage and the unresolved remainder.
- Ideal accepted-event oracle achieved exact full-hand answers where identifiable, with development full-hand coverage **4,692/10,424 =45.01%**. Oracle truth is grading evidence and cannot become model input.
- Under a standard eight-card FIFO cycle, two consecutive genuine play events with the same base identity can identify the second as Mirror only when the complete event ordering is reliable. Duplicate frames, swarms, generated troops, missed/same-tick plays and copies are not automatically distinct plays. Mirror level behavior does not justify assuming the copied card is higher-level than the preceding card. Historical Champion cycles, special modes and evolution readiness require separate qualification.
- Unknown/partial hands remain explicit. Estimates are uncertified; no hard legality mask, forced counter holding or invented unseen identity follows from an estimate.

The final deployment floors in `PLAN.md` are stronger than the development filters:

- Same-code/runtime ghost wins: at least +2 percentage points versus fresh R1e,
  paired 95% confidence lower bound above zero on independent final scenarios.
- Reactive wins: at least +8pp versus R1e, paired 95% lower bound above zero, at
  least 192 predeclared matched games, with no opponent-family regression.
- Rocket: at least +10pp aimed-action agreement; at least 50% correct one-Rocket
  finishes on at least 30 independent windows; improve two-Rocket finishing and
  defensive net value; materially increased waste/false fires are disqualifying.
- Damage-lead cycling, late/tiebreak outcomes, phase/matchup response and punishment
  after blocked offensive X-Bows require their own preregistered useful effects,
  denominators and paired uncertainty.
- Rocket-then-Tornado: at least +10pp joint sequence agreement plus demonstrated
  useful defensive combinations on adequate independent evidence.
- Barrel: at least 75% fewer wrong-lane fired Logs and +15pp correct gated lane
  responses on at least 100 unambiguous independent opportunities, with actual
  public landing interpretation verified separately.
- Each spawner family: at least +5pp action agreement with supporting paired
  uncertainty, plus improved defense outcomes. No family hidden by pooling.
- X-Bow: repeated useful resource/tower/support outcomes in matched probes,
  preserving useful defense. General card decline <=0.5pp, legal/public inputs and
  stable latency. Sampling/area aim require a same-checkpoint deterministic control.

These requirements remain open. A handoff is an unfinished-work record; no partial
aggregate, restored baseline, reader fix or startup check closes the objective.

No newwork is authorized by this registry itself. Currentownerstop/heartbeatpause
governs the transition. Dailynewsletter remainsa separatescheduler andsharedledger;
October5newsletterwasalreadydeliveredonceat21:37:21EDTin3HTTP200parts. Its later
scheduledheartbeatcorrectlyskippedthecompletedledger;latetriggercausewasunresolved.
Do notresendindividualmodelreportsornewsletters.

# Decisions Codex must not make -- for the owner/lead (newest last)

## 2026-10-03 15:38 EDT -- native area effects omitted, Rocket hit labels/behaviour coverage incomplete

- MEASURED source defect: native `effects` comes from the bridge's generic observed_effects list (jni_bridge.cpp:1988), while real area effects are separately exported at2099 as `area_effects`. replay_drive.py:452 records generic effects and discards area_effects. Three completed diagnostic re-drive samples have exact projectile-to-generic-effect aliases on every sampled frame and no area_effects field. Version4 now ignores generic aliases and refuses training with `native_area_effects_unavailable`. Earlier native_timing_evidence.json counted aliases as effects and is SUPERSEDED by native_source_audit.json.
- What: validate a corrected public area/timing recorder before any additional re-drive; choose whether/how to attribute Rocket tower hits from replay evidence and define the pro-context classifier's verified target labels. No new VM spending or live reader change authorized by this discovery.
- Evidence: `L70/gen_v31/native_source_audit.json`, `native_sample_mining_1510_v2/`, diagnostic receipt under `runs/rocket_native_samples_1510/`; bridge and recorder source above. Six near-tower Rocket flights in three native samples align with342-HP drops; that is compatible damage, not independent causal attribution. No universal497-HP damage threshold was applied to training.
- Legacy mining:14661 unique replays /9176 Rockets /5557 near-tower candidates,1349 multi-Rocket candidate sequences;157 duplicate-tag variants excluded in the same first-corpus order as dataset_gen. Most candidates are above497HP (5091/5557). These are geometric candidates, not all confirmed hits; full `_abil` mining is pending retrieval.
- Baseline gap: the pinned299 ghost logs measure Rocket share/play rate/elixir, but omit tower context, barrel flight/landing traces and final HP. The remaining five behaviour metrics are null/UNMEASURED in `behavior_baselines.json`. New instrumented baseline matches require resources and IPC currently unavailable while R1t/live run. The currently running R1t acceptance is unchanged; do not call it full updated behaviour acceptance.
- Options: (A) validate public recorder fields and add passive telemetry, then remeasure/fit on verified native data; (B) explicitly approve a documented proxy target (and its error audit) for the classifier. Recommendation:A. Keep gen_v3.1 training/live and R1e blocked; retain the required current live run and R1t.

## 2026-10-03 15:38 EDT -- publication retry denied

- Explicit scoped `git add` again failed creating `.git/index.lock` (Permission denied); staged diff remains empty. HEAD is lead commit `9e0b85b`. No commit or push occurred. A reviewed patch/manifest will be refreshed after the final evidence checkpoint. This is the same read-only metadata restriction, not a Git conflict.

## 2026-10-03 15:20 EDT -- required projectile timing is absent from source data

- What: complete and validate timing sources before the mandated gen_v3.1 retrain. No permission to omit the required timing inputs is inferred.
- Why: `research/sandbox_tools/replay_drive.py` snapshot stores six-column projectile rows and four-column effect rows, losing time-to-impact and remaining lifetime. `py.rs` PROJECTILE_FIELDS omits impact time; Flight.delay_ticks is pre-flight delay, not impact time. Reader v2 exposes target coordinates and effect remaining_ms, but no projectile time-to-impact. The ongoing VM job cannot retroactively recover discarded timing.
- Options: extend/validate public timing extraction and authorize any required additional re-drive cost; or approve a named public-trajectory estimate and its cross-source validation. Recommendation: validate a causal estimate using only observed motion before deciding whether another re-drive is necessary. Do not use future landing frames as model input or silently treat unknown as zero. This run retains unknown masks and rejects full training with missing timing.
- Evidence: `pipeline/projectile_observation.py`, `pipeline/tests/test_projectile_observation.py`, `research/sandbox_tools/replay_drive.py:438`, `research/ext/Royale/RoyaleSim/crates/royalesim/src/py.rs:310`, `scratchpad/gauntlet/L70/reader/FINDINGS.md`.

## 2026-10-03 15:20 EDT -- active R1t contention and publication restriction persist

- What: whether to change the resource allocation of the already-running R1t if live starvation persists. It was launched by the lead and its recipe/run directories remain untouched.
- Why: LIVE logs report median decisions 101-103 ms while R1t advances; this run has launched no GPU job. Changing/stopping the inherited training is an owner decision under the brief.
- Options: keep the lead's run; approve lower actor count/priority on a later launch; approve intervention. Recommendation: no additional heavy work, retain both required running jobs, and record the observed contention.
- Publication: this session still declares `.git` read-only with escalation disabled. The existing index.lock permission blocker remains; do not route the Git write through another tool to bypass it.
- Evidence: `L70/live/overnight.out`, `L70/rl/r1t_v3_gpu.out` u0010, current environment permissions; prior publication blocker.

## 2026-10-03 13:53 EDT -- ability intercepts do not establish both requested matches

- What: whether to allow a timing-dependent calibration (e.g. intercept plus age term), or accept declared residuals after intercept-only calibration. No calibration acceptance tolerance was registered. R1e and production ability-policy replacement remain blocked.
- Why: offline intercept candidates fitted on 11,728 non-test replay tags; evaluated on the existing 2,933 test tags. Fit-share residual at most 0.1241 pp, but heldout share residuals span -5.8175 to +6.7104 pp. Archer Queen presses 84.3% vs phase-1 79.6%, median all-press delay 7.60 s vs 10.65 s. Its paired delay change vs uncalibrated is only +0.25 s, 95% replay-bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.851]. Tombstone hero median 13.45 vs 10.575 s. These are reconstructed-board measurements, not engine-accepted presses or live performance.
- Options: (A) retain offline candidates and remeasure on ability-driven/native-id recordings; (B) approve adding a timing parameter and specify acceptable share/delay error; (C) approve these residuals explicitly. Recommendation: A, then B if residuals persist. Do not relax the R1e primary rule.
- Additional limits: phase-1 targets include test tags; denominator is inferred card deployments rather than confirmed eligible living controllers; Boss Bandit phase-1 all-press median is 11.65 s (first-press median 9.8 s). Existing phase-2 cadence/cooldown proxies are retained, not engine-validated.

- What: choosing either new checkpoint for ladder play remains the owner's decision, regardless of offline results.

# Lead rulings (owner unblocked all Tuesday items 2026-10-04 00:0x; the lead decides them now)

## R1. X-Bow labels (replaces the "Tuesday review" blocker of 2026-10-03 20:35 / 23:12) -- 2026-10-04 00:5x
Intent is read from GEOMETRY + PUBLIC tower state at the placement tick. No hidden state, no outcome peeking.
- OFFENSIVE X-Bow = at least one ALIVE enemy tower (princess or king) is inside X-Bow range from the placement:
  dist(X-Bow centre, tower centre) - tower collision radius <= X-Bow range. Take range and radii from the engine /
  card catalog constants (not hand-typed numbers), and print them in the label artifact.
- DEFENSIVE X-Bow = NO alive enemy tower in range, placement on the own half. Telemetry sub-flag `threat`: an enemy
  troop inside X-Bow range at the placement tick or within 5 s after (not part of the label).
- DEAD-LANE X-Bow = defensive by the rule above AND placed in the lane of a destroyed enemy princess tower (the owner's
  complaint). Telemetry only; it is the mistake the bot makes, not a pro target.
- VALIDATE the rule with the re-drive outcomes before using it: per label, the share of X-Bows that damaged an enemy
  tower during their lifetime (expect high for offensive, ~0 for defensive) and share that damaged troops. Report the
  12 boards of XBOW_REVIEW.md under the rule. If offensive-but-never-hit-a-tower is > 30%, stop and tell the lead.
- Offensive placement DIVERSITY (owner Tuesday item, now): behaviour metric = number of distinct lock-on cells used
  (and their entropy) per side/lane, pros vs bot, on the same tower states.

## R2. Rocket outcome labels (no native damage hook) -- 2026-10-04 00:0x
See TICKET "OWNER CHANGE OF PLAN": landing tick/point from the projectile's last observation + the Rocket area-effect
start (area timers give the exact start tick even at --k 10); tower hit = tower HP drop at landing +-2 ticks with the
tower inside the Rocket radius; troop hits = enemy entities inside the radius at landing (count, nominal elixir, HP
drop). Multi-Rocket cycling = >= 2 own Rockets on the same enemy tower within one match phase; tiebreak cycling =
tower Rockets while crowns are level in the last 60 s or overtime.

## R3. Re-drive granularity -- 2026-10-04 00:4x (measured on the VM, 4 slots in parallel, 3 replays each)
--k 10: 6.5 s/replay, 0.9 MB; --k 4: 12.7 s, 2.0 MB; --k 2: 21.6 s; --k 1: 37 s. Chosen: --k 10. Every projectile
row carries its target point, so time-to-impact is exact from ONE frame (distance to target / projectile speed);
past-motion TTI remains the live fallback when the reader lacks a target. The full observation before every play is
recorded regardless of k. Build every TTI/area feature so it works at k = 10 (the live reader runs at its own rate).

## R2b. Rocket hits at K=10 (answer to your ±2-tick coverage concern) -- 2026-10-04 01:0x
A landed Rocket damages EVERYTHING inside its radius at impact (engine mechanic, no misses). So the hit label is
GEOMETRIC inclusion at the landing tick: the landing tick comes from the area-effect start (exact even at K=10), and
unit/tower positions at that tick are linearly interpolated between the bracketing frames (<= 10 ticks apart; towers
do not move). The HP drop between the bracketing frames is CONFIRMATION only (report the share confirmed), never the
gate. Do not leave hits unknown just because no frame sits within ±2 ticks.

# October 3 re-drive and training omissions

Owner request: identify what was missed, which work stage owned it, why checks missed it, and the checks required before the next run. This is an evidence-based allocation by artifact ownership, not a claim about anyone's intent.

| Requested item | What happened and evidence | Responsible work stage | Why the old check missed it | Required correction/check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ability presses in IL boards | Original `replay_drive.py` skipped ability commands. HANDOFF's 11:1x claim that they were driven was retracted at 11:5x. Native ability re-drive later recorded 40,496 accepted activations with matching controllers. | Lead's original re-drive specification/claim and validation; Codex must not repeat the unverified claim in downstream checks. | Presence of ability events in input was mistaken for successful engine execution. | Sample accepted and rejected events; verify controller identity and before/after public effects, and account for every skipped event. |
| Exact evolved/hero unit inputs | Earlier body names folded forms to base; gen_v3 reconstructed forms conservatively. Original reader filtered evolved bodies. | Lead's original train/live contract; Codex's later adapter/integration verification. | Card vocabulary and tensor shapes were tested without checking exact native form IDs in real train/SIM/live frames. | Trace native ID -> base card plus form -> token -> model on base, evolution and hero controls in all three adapters. |
| Separate spell area effects | Lead's `_abil` job requested `--record-full`, but recorder saved generic `effects`, an alias of projectiles, and dropped bridge `area_effects`. Codex's initial `native_timing_evidence.json` counted these aliases as real effects; corrected by `native_source_audit.json`. | Lead's re-drive specification/preflight and recorder integration; Codex's initial source-semantic audit. | Nonempty arrays and names passed; nobody required a Poison/Tornado example with a distinct area identity and visible lifetime. | Compare raw bridge area export with saved frame and final model token; forbid projectile aliases; distinguish missing from present-empty. |
| Compiled native bridge and timer semantics | The first October3 overnight sample still had no area export: the VM binary was older than the source. Rebuilding exposed areas, then measured 44/44 adjacent area counters decreasing50ms per tick in the first replay, contradicting the source's elapsed-time interpretation. | Lead's bridge source/runtime deployment validation; Codex's initial continuation inspected source without first binding the running binary hash. | A current source checkout was treated as evidence about the loaded binary; arithmetic alone accepted an inverted lifetime. | Record source, built binary and deployed binary hashes; require actual raw fields from the running engine; verify timer direction and disappearance endpoints before any full re-drive. |
| Rocket causal troop/tower hits | The original recorder retained flight/aim and sparse boards but no source-linked damage/impact events. Census found geometric candidates, not causal hits. | Lead's re-drive requirements/validation; Codex's first mining scope only covered tower candidates and did not deliver troop/combo coverage until the amended brief was discovered. | Correlated HP drops and near-tower aims cannot exclude simultaneous damage. Sparse frames cannot recover missed events. | Versioned event ledger with source projectile/card, target, event tick and damage; engine-hit hook validation on isolated and competing-damage controls. Until then label geometric proxies explicitly and audit errors. |
| Time-to-impact | Recorder kept six projectile columns; SIM and reader exposed positions/targets but no verified TTI. | Lead's field-level re-drive spec and cross-path contract; Codex's first v4 implementation left unknown masks without a runnable way to satisfy the full training requirement. | `record-full` was treated as a semantic guarantee; tensor parity on unknown values did not prove usable timing. | Past-only motion estimator with ambiguity masks, moving/stationary/receding controls and same-tick/future-invariance tests; separately score against held-out landing brackets, never feed future truth. Record high-cadence source evidence in new drive. |
| Public-only opponent elixir | Legacy `obs_contract.from_engine` and dataset builder retain true opponent elixir in scalar columns 5/6; gen_v1/v2/v3 inherit it. Live counter being public did not make the IL dataset public. | Lead's original dataset/input contract; Codex's inherited-path audit caught it late and initially only checked a prefix of one stored dataset. | Train/live shape parity and score regressions can pass while provenance differs. | Inventory datasets/checkpoint lineage/results; relabel affected claims; mutate every private input and require unchanged new-model features; retain a legacy positive control. Compare counter vs truth only in a separate audit output. |
| Rocket behaviour beyond one-shot finishes | Initial finish-only weighting did not cover multi-Rocket cycling, tower-HP lead/tiebreak, defensive Rockets or both Tornado orders. | Codex's stopped-run weighting implementation; lead/owner amendments define the corrected scope. | The narrow <=497 HP conversion metric was used as a substitute for the broader request. | Requirement-to-label/weight/metric matrix, six joint context targets, full distributions, no scripted Rocket action threshold. |
| X-Bow context and defensive label | Initial acceptance listed five behaviour gaps; X-Bow metrics were omitted until amendment reconciliation. Existing y>0.58 bucket is not a validated tactical label. | Codex's coverage inventory and inherited audit semantics; lead/owner retain ambiguous-label approval. | A geometry bucket was available and reports covered only the earlier scope. | Board-context examples stratified by placement, lane death, phase and follow-on Rocket; owner review before treating geometry as strategic defense. |
| Ability share AND timing calibration | Intercept-only candidates matched training share but not all delay targets; older extraction used non-ability-driven reconstructed boards. | Lead's initial calibration recipe; Codex's candidate fitting and evidence limitations. | One fitted statistic cannot certify two targets; phase-1 test-tag overlap and inferred eligible lifetimes weaken interpretation. | Remeasure native controller deployments/presses, fit intercept plus timing term on fit tags, report held-out share and first/all-press delay error per ability, preserve Boss Bandit semantics. |
| Full behaviour acceptance | Existing ghost outputs omit tower/flight/landing timelines; full updated metrics cannot be reconstructed from action totals. | Lead's original acceptance telemetry; Codex's completion claims must explicitly retain missing metrics. | Existing successful ghost/reactive runs were mistaken for coverage of newly requested behaviours. | Instrument and test each metric before launching paired baseline runs; missing is null, not zero, and partial acceptance cannot authorize deployment. |

## Mandatory preflight before any re-drive, dataset build or training

1. Freeze a requirement matrix: each requested field/label/metric has source, units, visibility, serialization, adapter, tensor and consumer; assign a positive and negative sample to every row. Re-read current TICKET and owner amendments immediately before launch.
2. Pin source/code hashes and use a NEW output directory. Preserve `_abil` corpora and old runs. Confirm one GPU job, live health, CPU budget, disk space and scoped authorization.
3. Run twenty deliberately selected replays covering Rockets on towers/troops, both Tornado orders, area spells, both Barrel types, abilities and native forms. Twenty arbitrary successes do not prove coverage. Fail if required coverage is absent.
4. Check every frame's schema, finite/range/unit constraints, identity continuity, monotone time and absent-vs-empty exports. Account for successful/failed/skipped commands and match summary tags to replay files.
5. Validate semantics against independent evidence: actual area expiration, flight/impact, isolated and simultaneous damage, native form IDs and ability controller effects. Schema-only or mocked tests do not certify engine semantics. Keep proxies and causal truth in separate fields.
6. Build a small version-4 dataset from those exact samples; trace each required field into a nonpadding tensor value. Independently mutate opponent hand/next/elixir/deck forms/internal ability readiness and require byte-identical model inputs. Own hand and visible effects remain permitted.
7. Feed equivalent public frames through training/SIM/reader adapters and compare tensors. Check orientation, same-tick observations, missing fields, unknown timing, overflow and future invariance. Require v1/v2/v3 default byte parity.
8. Verify replay-disjoint fit/tune/test tags; fit context weights only on fit, choose the knob on tune, report test once. Ensure all six context targets and all behaviour metrics are represented; no omission hidden by aggregate loss.
9. Dry-run a small forward/backward pass and an instrumented acceptance replay before the full build/train. Confirm actual input tensor use, finite losses, all required metrics and paired seed identities. Pin recipe/AMP settings and record results with play rates and CIs.
10. Only promote after all mandatory checks pass. A missing VM/IP, unvalidated native hit hook, ambiguous X-Bow label or missing field is a specific unresolved gate. Report it without claiming the whole plan is done. Publish scoped code/evidence, HANDOFF and JOURNAL; do not stage `icebow/data`.

Current owner decisions authorize proxies plus their error audit, causal motion estimates, native recalibration followed by a timing term, and the public-only retrain. They do not turn unvalidated native fields into verified truth. New VM start/IP and ambiguous X-Bow label approval remain external dependencies. Git publication remains restricted by this session's read-only `.git` permission.

# CODEX BRIEF -- continue ClashBot until Claude's usage resets (Tuesday 2026-10-06)

Written by the lead (Claude) on 2026-10-04 (final update ~20:55 EDT). Read this file first, then `README.md` (the project overview) and the TOP of
`HANDOFF.md` (the blocks dated 2026-10-04: every number below comes from there, with its context). The owner will talk
to you directly. This brief tells you what was done, what was measured, what to do next, and -- most important -- HOW
the work is done here, so the project does not drift.

## 1. How we work (non-negotiable; this is what keeps the project on course)

1. **Measure, then claim.** Every claim is labelled *measured* (cite the number + file), *untested* (say so, propose the
   measurement) or *contradicted* (give the evidence). Never present a guess as a result. The owner is a student who
   asks to be corrected: if the owner's diagnosis or idea is wrong or untested, say so plainly, with evidence, before
   acting on it.
2. **Acceptance instruments, not impressions.** A model or setting is better only on:
   - the **paired ghost screen** (`scratchpad/gauntlet/L68/generalist/screen_gen/run_screen.py`, 299 pinned replays,
     flags exactly as in `scratchpad/gauntlet/L71/gen_v31/accept_v31a.sh`: `--split train --noise-off all --opp-elixir
     counter --action-delay 26 --extrapolate 26 --seeds 0 --device cuda --forms-mode deck --tau 0.27 --only-tags-from
     scratchpad/gauntlet/L68/generalist/lat26/screens/train_C.jsonl --behaviour-telemetry`), scored with `--pair A B`
     (paired pp with a 95% bootstrap CI), AND
   - **reactive play** (`python -m pipeline.search_s0 --seeds 0:24 --opps gen,s1 --arms plain ...`, wins out of 24), AND
   - the **behaviour telemetry** (Rocket share, tower Rockets, finish-offs, multi-Rocket cycles, defensive Rockets, both
     Rocket/Tornado orders, X-Bow cells/lanes, pre-emptive Log) -- compare with the pro baselines in HANDOFF.
   Always pair against a baseline run with the SAME code (a code change between two screens invalidates the pairing --
   see the R8 mistake in HANDOFF 14:5x). Write the decision rule BEFORE you see the result.
3. **One change per experiment.** Each run changes one thing so its effect is attributable. New behaviour goes behind an
   opt-in flag/config key whose default is byte-identical to today, with a test proving that.
4. **No hand-written playstyles.** The owner's rule: the bot learns from pros (imitation from re-driven pro replays,
   weighting of pro situations, RL). Do not add rules like "Rocket when tower < X HP". The only hand-written rule
   allowed is the owner-ordered interim Hero Ice Wizard ability rule (`hero_button.py`), until pro data exists.
5. **Public information only.** The opponent's hand, next card, elixir and ability readiness are NEVER model inputs.
   Measurements may use recorded hidden state; models may not.
6. **Machine discipline.** One GPU job at a time (check `nvidia-smi` and running python first). The laptop is shared.
   Never kill or edit a running script (write a `_v2` file instead). Kill processes only by exact command-line match in
   a command that does not itself contain the pattern. Long jobs: write a launcher script, log to a file, poll it.
7. **Live play.** Never start, stop or reconfigure live unless the owner asks (the owner starts it with
   `bash scratchpad/gauntlet/L70/live/start_live.sh`, stops with `stop_live.sh`; the model is the path in
   `scratchpad/gauntlet/L70/live/CKPT_OVERRIDE`). Never deploy a checkpoint without the owner's explicit approval:
   post "APPROVAL NEEDED: <what>" to Discord with the evidence and wait.
8. **Owner decisions.** Anything the owner would decide (deploys, live settings, spending, deleting data, changing an
   acceptance rule, changing the experiment plan) -> write it to `.foreman/codex_autopilot/BLOCKERS.md` (what, why,
   options, your recommendation, evidence) and continue with unblocked work. Do not decide it yourself.
9. **Record everything.** After every change batch: update `HANDOFF.md` (a dated block at the top, numbers + paths),
   commit and push to `main` with a clear message ending `Co-Authored-By: Codex (autopilot)`. NEVER stage `icebow/data/`
   (secrets incl. `discord_webhook.txt`; never print the webhook URL). Post a short Discord report after each milestone
   (`icebow/.venv/Scripts/python.exe scratchpad/gauntlet/L69/discord/post.py <msg.txt>`): what was done, the numbers and
   what they mean, next steps.
10. **Stay in scope.** Do the queue in section 4. No refactors, no new frameworks, no re-auditing finished work, no long
    reports. If a gate blocks you, try the obvious fix first, then record the question and move to the next item.

## 2. State at the time of writing (2026-10-04 ~15:50 EDT)

- **Data:** full real-engine re-drive of 14,818 pro recordings (0 failures) with public observations: projectiles +
  time-to-impact, spell areas + timers, exact evo/hero ids, driven abilities. Dataset
  `icebow/data/pipeline/gen_dataset_v31_public.npz`: 3,517,863 rows, 14,661 replays, 4,283 decks, v3val 12,237.
- **Imitation models (feature version 4):** gen_v3.1a (inputs only), 3.1b (+ six-target pro-context weighting 2.0),
  3.1c (weight 4.0). **gen_v3.1c is the best gen model**: vs 3.1b +1.2 [-2.2, +4.5]; vs live-best RL u0155 -1.7
  [-4.7, +1.3]; reactive gen 13/24, S1 19/24.
- **R8 (look-ahead advances projectiles/effects, inference-only):** measured on 3.1a: pre-emptive Log 23.5% -> 49.8%
  (pros 39.1% same deck/definition); ghost +1.0 [-1.7, +3.7]. On by default for v4.
- **RL:** R1e = PPO from gen_v3.1c (5 actors, evo/hero census opponents, calibrated per-ability press models v2,
  R8), launched 15:06 by `scratchpad/gauntlet/L71/rl/run_r1e_v3.sh`; log `scratchpad/gauntlet/L71/rl/r1e.log`. Its
  verdict and the live decision are appended in section 6 when they arrive.
- **Live:** RUNNING on R1e u0155 (owner decision, to observe the new inputs live) -- see section 6. Start/stop: `start_live.sh` / `stop_live.sh`.
- **Abilities in the sim:** `ability_policy: v2` (royale_env / e1_eval / rl_royale / search_s0 `--ability-policy`).
  Calibrated models: `scratchpad/gauntlet/L70/abilities/ability_models_v2.json` (held-out share error <= 3 pp for 17/22).
- **Live ability:** Hero Ice Wizard = owner's interim rule (freeze clumps of >= 3 troops, or a win condition on our
  half when Tesla is not in hand / < 4 elixir). Reader v2 reports hero units as 203000000 + n (fixed lookup).

## 3. Findings that steer the next steps (all measured; files in HANDOFF)

- **Rocket is the biggest gap:** ~0.9% of plays vs pros ~5.8%; tower Rockets ~8-10 per 299 games; finish-offs 0;
  multi-Rocket cycles 0. Weighting 2x/4x barely moved it. Diagnosis (`scratchpad/gauntlet/L71/rocket_diag/`): at pro
  Rocket moments the model gives Rocket P = .24 (AUC .84, well calibrated) but **argmax** picks it only 22%; the gate is
  not the blocker (87% pass); and when Rocket IS chosen the **argmax cell hits a tower only 28.5%** (overtime-behind
  6.9%) because the cell distribution mixes troop and tower targets.
- **X-Bow:** pros use 2 offensive rows and ~24 cells; the model's distribution is spread (80% mass on lock-capable cells)
  but argmax collapses it to 2 cells; sampling X-Bow cells lowered agreement (not adopted). Dead-lane X-Bows: pros' are
  mostly POCKET plays; the bot's are mostly own-half (n = 30, weak). X-Bow reach for labels = 13.0384 tiles
  centre-to-centre (98.2% hit recall).
- **RL so far never increased Rocket use** (u0155 50 Rockets vs gen_v1 72 in the same 299 games). Hypothesis
  (untested): sampled Rockets with poor aim waste elixir, so RL learns to avoid them -- fix aim before expecting RL to help.
- **RL determinism:** results are now sorted before learning (actor count / timing no longer change runs).

## 4. Next steps (do in this order)

- **Q1 (CPU) Card choice: CONFIDENCE-FILTERED sampling, opt-in -- never plain sampling.** Owner concern (2026-10-04,
  correct): plain sampling over the hand would sometimes play a card the model itself rates as unviable when the top
  card is the only good answer (the diagnosis already shows plain T=1 sampling firing Rocket on 7.6% of non-Rocket pro
  moments). Design (`card_choice: argmax | filtered`, `card_ratio r`, `card_T T`; default argmax, byte-identical,
  test), in `pipeline/e1_eval.py` `live_decide` (SIM) and `pipeline/live_gen.py` (live):
  1. Only affordable hand cards are candidates (the existing mask).
  2. **Keep the argmax card whenever the model is confident:** a card is a candidate only if p_card >= r * p_top
     (r = 0.5 / 0.7 to test). If no other card passes, play the top card exactly as today. So a clear "only answer"
     (e.g. p_top .9) can never be replaced; only near-ties are randomised.
  3. Sample among the remaining candidates with temperature T (0.7 / 1.0), seeded (SIM: per match seed; live: logged).
  4. The play/wait gate stays deterministic (P(play) > tau). The cell rule is unchanged (Q2 handles spell cells).
  **Offline check BEFORE any SIM time** (CPU, extend `scratchpad/gauntlet/L71/rocket_diag/rocket_diag.py`, teacher-
  forced pro val rows of the icebow deck): for each (r, T) report (a) Rocket recall on pro-Rocket rows, (b) Rocket
  false-fire on non-Rocket rows, (c) overall card agreement with the pro (expected value) vs argmax, (d) **override
  rate on confident rows** (rows where argmax prob >= .6: must be ~0), (e) the share of decisions that change at all.
  Drop any (r, T) whose overall agreement falls more than 1 pp below argmax. Only the survivors go to Q3.
- **Q2 (CPU) Area-aware spell aim, opt-in.** For area spells, choose the cell that maximises the model's cell-probability
  mass inside the spell's catalog radius instead of the single argmax cell (same flag pattern, SIM + live). Test: a
  sharp off-target cell vs a broad on-tower cluster must pick the cluster.
- **Q3 (GPU, only when no other GPU job runs)** ghost-screen A/Bs on the live model (or gen_v3.1c), paired against its
  saved screen run with the SAME code: (a) the best filtered-sampling setting from Q1's offline check, (b) the
  second best, (c) area aim, (d) area aim + (a). Report win value CIs, reactive play (gen + S1, 24 seeds each) and the
  behaviour telemetry. **Adoption rule (pre-registered; the owner's performance concern):** an option is proposed for
  live ONLY if (1) its paired ghost point estimate is >= 0 vs the baseline (not just "CI touches 0"), (2) reactive wins
  are not lower than the baseline's by more than 2 of 48, and (3) Rocket use / tower-Rocket hits move toward the pro
  numbers. If Rocket use rises but win value falls, it is REJECTED (report it; do not tune until it passes). Then
  "APPROVAL NEEDED: enable <option> live?" -- the owner decides.
- **Q4** Re-run the diagnostics (`scratchpad/gauntlet/L71/rocket_diag/rocket_diag.py`,
  `scratchpad/gauntlet/L70/xbow_diversity/xbow_diversity.py`) on the live model and report what changed.
- **Q5 Small fixes:** `pipeline/tests/test_dataset_spool.py` (KeyError 'own_ability' in the model_gen mmap path);
  `scratchpad/gauntlet/L70/live/run_live.sh` `last_stop()` should also match "new checkpoint deployed" (edit only if no
  run_live.sh process is running; otherwise make `run_live_v2.sh`).
- **Not for you (owner/lead):** the Hero Ice Wizard pro-data crawl (RoyaleAPI needs the owner's Cloudflare click);
  any deploy; R1e follow-up RL runs (propose them in BLOCKERS with a one-change design; do not launch).

## 5. Where things are

`README.md` (pipeline + how to run), `HANDOFF.md` (state, numbers, traps), `.foreman/codex_autopilot/LEAD_RULINGS.md`
(the lead's rulings R1-R8 on labels, TTI, look-ahead -- follow them), `scratchpad/gauntlet/L71/` (today's scripts and
outputs: gen_v31/, rl/, rocket_diag/, barrel_log/), `pipeline/` (all model/data/sim/RL code, tests in
`pipeline/tests/`; run with `research/ext/Royale/.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest`).

## 6. R1e verdict and live decision (final, 2026-10-04 ~20:55 EDT)

R1e = `icebow/data/bench/rl_royale/rseries_r1e31/rseries_r1e31_u{0080,0155}.pt` (base gen_v3.1c). All measured
(`scratchpad/gauntlet/L71/rl/r1e.log`, `r1e_accept/`):

| model | ghost vs gen_v3.1c | ghost vs old u0155 | reactive gen/S1 (old census) | reactive gen/S1 (evo/hero census, abilities v2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1e u0155 | +1.3 [-1.7, +4.3] | -0.3 [-3.3, +2.7] | 17 / 21 | 11 / 21 |
| R1e u0080 | -0.3 [-3.3, +2.7] | -2.0 [-5.4, +1.3] | 16 / 21 | 11 / 21 |
| gen_v3.1c | 0 | -1.7 [-4.7, +1.3] | 13 / 19 | 8 / 19 |
| old rseries_r1_u0155 | -- | 0 | 14 / 24 | 12 / 24 |

Reading: RL on top of gen_v3.1c helped (R1e beats its base on all three instruments) and nearly closes the gap to the
old RL model, but does not beat it in the simulator: a tie on the ghost screen and the old census (38/48 each), and
old u0155 wins the evo/hero census 36/48 vs 32/48 (mostly vs S1: 24 vs 21).

**OWNER DECISION 2026-10-04 ~21:00: LIVE = R1e `icebow/data/bench/rl_royale/rseries_r1e31/rseries_r1e31_u0155.pt`**
(CKPT_OVERRIDE), "mainly to observe if our input space change and fixes translated into better live performance" --
simulator ties do not settle live performance. Do NOT switch live back on your own; the owner decides.

**Implications for your queue:**
- **Q0 (new, first, CPU) Live comparison, R1e vs old u0155.** From the live logs
  (`scratchpad/gauntlet/L68/live_reader/live_play_*.jsonl`, `scratchpad/gauntlet/L70/live/overnight.out` results +
  the checkpoint each run loaded -- "checkpoint override" lines / process --ckpt), tabulate per checkpoint: matches,
  wins/losses with a Wilson 95% CI, trophies over time, and live behaviour (Rocket share of plays, pre-emptive Logs vs
  barrels, ability presses, X-Bow placements) from the play/frame events. Old u0155 has ~2 days of live matches on
  10-03/10-04 as the baseline. Report every ~30 R1e matches (Discord, short); say plainly when the CI cannot separate
  them yet. Measurement only -- never change live.
- Run Q3 on R1e u0155 (the live model) AND old u0155, each paired against its own fresh baseline screen made with the
  SAME code (first produce `--behaviour-telemetry` baseline screens for both -- the old u0155 screen in L70/rl/r1_accept
  has no telemetry).
- Any further RL run (e.g. R1e for more updates, or RL after the Rocket fixes) is an owner/lead decision: propose it in
  BLOCKERS.md with a one-change design, do not launch it.

# Discord reporting

Owner instruction, October 5, 2026: use plain wording, cover the relevant work,
explain findings and their interpretation, state verdicts and next steps, and
make sections easy to distinguish. The owner's supplied newsletter brief is a
style reference, not a script to copy or authority to change server settings.

## Writing each update

Write for a reader who has not followed this repository. Use a short dated title,
bold section labels, blank lines, and brief paragraphs or bullets. Explain model
nicknames on first use. Avoid packed slash-separated counts, unexplained gate
codes, receipt dumps, and technical shorthand. Keep detailed provenance locally.

Adapt these sections to the actual news; do not fill an empty template:

- **Work completed:** what changed or was tested, and why. Include relevant data,
  simulator, live-play, diagnosis, tooling, and evaluation work, not only training.
- **What we found:** a few useful numbers with denominators and named comparisons.
  For model results include R1e and the immediate control under comparable inputs
  and runtime. Distinguish training, recorded-action agreement, simulator games,
  and live games. Give uncertainty when measured; do not invent it.
- **What it means:** explain what the result supports, what remains uncertain,
  and whether a proposed cause is measured or still a hypothesis. Separate PLAY
  from WAIT gains when aggregate agreement could mislead. Coordinate agreement,
  physical damage, and winning games are different measurements.
- **Decision:** accepted, rejected, still running, or blocked, with the reason.
  State deployment status explicitly. An engineering check passing is not a
  stronger-model claim. Preserve all existing acceptance criteria and failures.
- **Next:** the next concrete test or action and the question it should answer.
  Identify a proposal as untested and an active job as active.

Be concise without dropping material failures or contradictory findings. Group
related experiments instead of listing every receipt. A short update may merge
sections. Longer posts may use numbered parts, split at paragraph boundaries.
Do not copy the supplied document or retrofit/resend already delivered reports.

## Daily edition

Send one newsletter every day at **9:30 PM America/New_York** (Eastern local
time, including daylight saving changes), through the existing owner's webhook.
This is directly authorized: no recurring draft-approval request is required.
The daily reporting schedule continues after the temporary improvement-worker
cutoff and Claude's return; it does not authorize more training or live play.

Use the latest HANDOFF, dated reviews, verified results, delivery receipts, and
relevant changes since the prior edition's cutoff. The first edition covers the
preceding 24 hours. Include unfinished work and the current live/deployment
status. Include ladder results/trophy changes or one or two clip links only when
verified records actually provide them. Never invent activity or imply missing
data is zero. On a quiet day, send a brief truthful status instead of recycled
news. Previously reported model results can be summarized as part of the day's
roundup, but must not be sent again as new individual model reports.

Save the actual newsletter as `reports/discord/newsletters/YYYY-MM-DD.md`, using
the Eastern date, plus a same-stem `.sources.json` containing the reporting
window, source paths/hashes, and claim-to-source notes. This evidence stays local;
the audience receives readable findings rather than internal paths and hashes.

## Sending and delivery records

For new reports use the companion sender below. It reads the **same existing
webhook configuration** as `scratchpad/gauntlet/L69/discord/post.py`; the old sender
and its historical hashes remain unchanged. Do not create a new webhook, alter
channels, inspect/display its secret, or post through another route.

```powershell
research/ext/Royale/.venv/Scripts/python.exe scratchpad/gauntlet/L69/discord/send_report.py --id newsletter-YYYY-MM-DD --file reports/discord/newsletters/YYYY-MM-DD.md
```

For new individual reports use a stable unique ID such as `model-MODEL-final`.
Check existing historical receipts too: a new sender ID does not authorize a
duplicate of an old delivered report. Existing frozen jobs with their bound
sender must not be edited while active; apply the writing guide to their report
drafts and preserve their established receipts.

The companion saves exact text, hashes, per-part HTTP status and Discord message
IDs under `reports/discord/deliveries/ID/`. A completed ID is skipped. An incomplete
or ambiguous attempt stops for delivery reconciliation; never delete its record
or blindly resend. Successful earlier parts must not be duplicated. A draft alone
does not mean delivered. Keep records across Claude/Codex handoffs.

Before posting, check the draft against its sources and remove credentials,
webhook URLs, private setup details, other players' identifying names/tags, and
ping syntax. The sender also disables mentions. Do not infer server/channel
configuration from the supplied brief; use the existing destination unchanged.

## Scheduler ownership

The Codex thread heartbeat named **ClashAI daily newsletter** owns the daily send.
Its automation ID is recorded at the top of HANDOFF. Claude should follow this
writing guide for all new reports, and must not install a second daily scheduler
or manually duplicate a completed edition. If scheduler ownership is transferred,
disable the old schedule first and retain the same dated delivery records.
Local scheduled execution requires the machine and Codex app to be running.

# Gates: overnight ClashBot fix queue (2026-08-24 -> 25)

OWNS: HANDOFF.md, icebow/src/clashrl/**, icebow/config/config.yaml, icebow/tests/**

Scope: train a matched control arm and a fixes-2+3 arm at 3600 episodes from the same init,
then evaluate fixes 1, 2+3 and 4 against that control with >=30 matches per arm and a
pre-committed 2-sigma bar, recording an honest verdict for each -- including "no measurement".

AMENDED 2026-08-24 (throughput, recorded rather than silently applied). Measured 0.30 ep/s, so two
3600-episode arms would take ~6.7 h of the ~9 available and leave no room for the adjustment round
the owner explicitly asked for. The control run passes THROUGH 2600 on its way to 3600, so it is
snapshotted there: that buys the matched three-way point (fix1@2600 / fix23@2600 / control@2600)
from ONE control run, and the fixes-2+3 arm then needs only 2600 episodes. G2's bar moved 3600 ->
2600 for that reason. fix1 vs control is ALSO evaluated at 3600, where both arms already exist, so
nothing is lost -- only bought.

AMENDED AGAIN 2026-08-25 (G1: 3600 -> 2600, against ARM_control_at2600.pt). `--matches N` in this
trainer means N EPISODES, not N matches -- the control was launched with `--matches 2850` and
stopped cleanly at 2850 EPISODES / 2172 real matches, so 3600 was never reachable from that launch.
The bar moves to the artifact the comparisons ACTUALLY use: ARM_control_at2600.pt, a true
2600-episode snapshot, which is what fix 1 was already evaluated against and what fixes 2+3 will be.
Nothing is weakened -- every comparison is still matched at 2600 -- but the 3600 figure was wrong
and is not left standing.

AMENDED 2026-08-25 (G3 and G7, reasons recorded). Both originally asserted HISTORICAL facts against
MUTABLE tree state, so both flipped to FAIL the moment fixes 2+3 were correctly reverted for failing
their effect criterion -- i.e. they punished the right action. G3 now proves the arm ran patched code
from its OWN probe dump (xbow_defends/xbow_no_lock cannot exist unpatched), which is durable evidence
that does not depend on what the tree looks like later. G7's original wording ("green WITH fixes 2+3
applied") was verified and PASSED at 628 tests while the patch was in; its purpose -- "the change does
not break the suite" -- was met and is recorded in 4f. It now asserts the tree AS SHIPPED is green,
which is a claim about a different and more relevant artifact, not a softened version of the old one.

NOTE ON WHAT THESE GATES ASSERT. The deliverable is a SOUND EVALUATION, not a favourable one.
A fix that measurably fails still satisfies its gate. Gates that demanded "fix passes" would
create pressure to fit the analysis to the gate, which is the exact failure this ledger exists
to prevent.

## L66k (2026-09-07) -- TRAP: pgrep/pkill -f match their OWN shell; a "wedged process" I reported twice never existed
- `pgrep -fc s3_teacher.py` run over ssh matches the remote bash shell itself, because the pattern appears in that shell's command line. It therefore NEVER returns 0 while you are asking, and its floor of 1 is the question, not an answer.
- Consequence (c): I twice told the owner in chat that the teacher run had "wedged at 497/500 with one process resident". There was no such process -- the residual 1 was my own ssh shell every time, and both full-bench runs had actually completed. The claim never reached HANDOFF, GAUNTLET_LOG or any Discord report, so nothing written needs retracting, but it was wrong when said.
- Same root cause broke two launches: `pkill -f s3_teacher.py` and then `pkill -f "v3_sh"` each killed the very shell issuing them (the pattern is in its own argv), so the command died before its own `echo LAUNCHED` and returned completely silently -- a launch that fails with no output at all.
- Reliable forms: `ps -eo pid,args | grep "[s]3_teacher"` for counting (the bracket stops the literal from matching its own regex) and never pkill by a pattern that appears in the issuing command line.

## L66l (2026-09-07) -- horizon hypothesis DEAD (rollout saturates); all three cheap explanations eliminated

Lengthening buys 0.74 tiles then nothing, against a ~5-tile gap to the student. Retires the "x-bow payoff accrues over tens of seconds" reasoning -- 120 s is most of a match.

With 5cs.90's oracle check (1.68 tiles available, 13.5 chosen), the finding is localised: a greedy single-placement rollout scored on engine damage does not pick pro placements, and it is not resolution, reachability, tie-breaking, the unit term, the opponent, or the horizon.
- What is left is not a bug: (1) SEQUENCING -- pro placements are setup for the next card and no single-placement objective can represent that; testing means searching over action sequences, a rebuild. (2) THE TARGET -- 5cs.53's gate assumed placements that win engine exchanges are the placements pros make; three nulls plus the oracle check are consistent with those being different objectives (elixir economy, cycle, tower-race position). If (2) holds, pro agreement is the wrong gate for S3 rather than the teacher being broken.
- Recommendation: stop patching the objective; the cheap space is exhausted. Owner call posted. My reading favours (2) -- the student reaches 21.9-23.9% by imitation while search reaches 0% while demonstrably able to propose the pro's cell.

## L67g-h (2026-09-08 18:00-21:00 UTC) -- the freeze, the ceiling, and two live repairs
- **Owner report "the model can freeze up mid-match": REAL and now explained.** 600 decisions / 70 plays over 4 matches; not a hang (WAIT lines print throughout) and the RATE is right (9.1 plays/min vs a pro's 8-10.5) -- the distribution is not: ~50 s stretches at 8-10 elixir with 0 plays.
- **RETRACTED mid-loop:** "the gate ignores elixir", read off play.py's WAIT lines. WAIT is `p < tau`, so the sample is truncated at the threshold and conditioned on the outcome. Engine VAL says the gate is CALIBRATED in elixir (0.046->0.472 vs pro 0.037->0.490); live frames, unconditioned, say the same (p 0.109 -> 0.567 across elixir 0-3 -> 9-10).
- **Cause found, and it was mine:** supplying the opponent-elixir estimate (wired last loop) cuts the live play rate up to 3.2x (frames over tau: 0.278 none / 0.156 at opp 5 / 0.087 at opp 10), and the estimator RATCHETS upward on every missed enemy play. Two repairs shipped, no retrain: `play.student_opp_elixir` default false, and the estimator now re-baselines on saturation (unit-checked: pinned 10 -> a detected Giant drops it to 5.0; pre-fix it stayed 10.0).
- **THE CEILING ON PRO AGREEMENT IS 27.5%** (40k pro plays, 2,238 replays, 157 players, pairs across different replays AND different players, blocked on same hand+card+elixir). ## L67cd (2026-09-18) -- ROOT CAUSE of both lost sessions: the capture grabs a SCREEN RECTANGLE, so any window on top IS what the bot sees
- **(a) Mechanism:** `capture.py:43-61` resolves the game's client area to a screen rect and `grab()` captures **that region of the screen**, not the window's pixels. Anything drawn over it is fed to the detector as if it were the game.
- **(a) What it actually captured:** `run.py diag` -> `data/diag_state.png` shows **a browser displaying the Claude Code conversation**, not Clash Royale. Hence `detect_state -> UNKNOWN` every frame; match_end templates 0.303/0.317 vs thr 0.80; the "Battle button best-match (0.570,0.866)" is a **spurious template hit on page content** vs configured tap [0.492,0.771]; and nav's reward tap (0.500,0.550) / dismiss (0.645,0.905) were **clicking the browser** for minutes. The owner's "can't find the battle button" = the bot was not looking at the game.
- **(a) SAME failure as the antivirus dialog (BO)** that killed 22 overnight relaunches -- another window over the same rectangle. **Two lost sessions, one root cause.** Not nav, not templates, not the model.
- Config is fine: `title_contains: "Clash Royale"`, `region: null` (auto-detect each refresh). Trap for later: pinning `window.region` short-circuits `refresh_region()` at `capture.py:44` and a stale rect can never self-correct.
- **(a) Not fixable in-process:** `SetForegroundWindow`/`ShowWindow` on the game handle failed (Windows blocks foreground-stealing from a background process -- same reason nav's force-focus fails). Synthetic window-rearranging input was declined on judgement (occluding window showed a purchase control) and, for the security dialog, blocked by the permission classifier.
- **PRE-FLIGHT, would have saved both sessions:** run `python run.py diag` and confirm `data/diag_state.png` shows the ACTUAL game before launching. `detect_state -> UNKNOWN` while on Home means the capture is hijacked -- do not launch. The game must stay on top and unobstructed for the whole run.
- Banked so far (**not** a winrate): **11 matches**, same ckpt/tau -- 9 from 01:13-01:40 (3W-6L) + 2 from 17:35-17:42 (1W-1L, both overtime). `score_live_baseline.py` pools them.
- **NOT established:** any live winrate; whether Home detects correctly once unobstructed (the only capture on disk is of the browser).


## L67ce (2026-09-18) -- the bot plays NOTHING, silently, when the in-game deck != the configured deck; an IN_MATCH health check does not catch it
- **(a) Symptom:** 5 ledger rows in ~7 min, durations **51/38/128/85/63 s**, outcomes LOSS 0-1 x3, 0-2, 0-1. None of those end a CR match (one tower down doesn't; 38 s can't three-crown). Decisive: **`taps=0`, `waits=0`** across all five.
- **(a) Cause:** `run.py diag` -> `data/diag_state.png` shows a **real match** (1:30 left, opp "ENZO PRO" 10000 trophies) but the hand holds **Fireball(4) + 1-cost + 6-cost + 3-cost** -- not icebow. `recognize_hand` matches nothing, `act_in_match` early-returns (`play.py:801`), and the bot stands still while a real opponent dismantles it.

- **(c) MY VERIFICATION TRAP:** my 6-min health check asserted `IN_MATCH > 0` and printed **"PLAYING OK"**. IN_MATCH was genuinely fine -- the bot *was* in matches. **The check must assert `taps > 0`.** A deck mismatch yields a perfectly healthy state machine driving a policy that never acts.
- **(c) Correction:** I first called those 5 rows "fabricated". **They are REAL losses** -- the bot genuinely lost because it played nothing. Invalid as a measure of the *policy*, not invalid as outcomes. Quarantined to `...180120.jsonl.INVALID`; the action was right, the first commit message's reasoning was not.
- **(a) Valid data intact:** scorer now reports **2 files / 11 matches** (9 + 2), 4W-7L, **CI [15.2%, 64.6%]** -- meaningless at n=11, recorded for traceability only. This also **exercised the multi-file pooling path for the first time** (previously only ever run on one file).
- **PRE-FLIGHT is now TWO checks:** (1) `run.py diag` and LOOK at the capture (BP, window-occlusion); (2) after launch confirm **`taps > 0`**, not `IN_MATCH > 0` (BQ, deck mismatch). Each alone would have saved a session.
- **NOT established:** why the active deck changed between 17:42 and 18:01; whether a tray-vs-`deck_keys` pre-launch check is feasible -- **not implemented** (`play.py:365-369` warns on checkpoint/deck mismatch, not on a TRAY mismatch).


## L67cf (2026-09-18) -- RETRACTION: I killed a HEALTHY run with a check that could never have passed
- **(c) MY ERROR.** The 3-min abort counted `[student] TAP`/`WAIT` in `icebow/data/play_<ts>.log`. **Those lines print straight to stdout and never go through `log()`, so they never appear in that file.** Control: the known-good 17:35 session played **2 complete matches** and its session log has **0 TAP lines in 20 lines total**. The check read zero regardless of performance -- it was structurally guaranteed to fire.
- **(a) What the run was really doing:** stdout capture `live_baseline_20260918_182802.log` (20,552 B) shows **26 TAPs, 21 WAITs**, cards `tesla_evo, skeletons, knight, x_bow, tornado, ice_wizard` -- **exactly the configured icebow deck**. Last tap **18:31:15.008**; my abort killed it at **18:31:15**. Mid-match, mid-play.
- **(c) Corrects `f8b3cdf` (§BQ):** that commit says the 18:28 run aborted on a deck mismatch. **Wrong.** The owner had already fixed the deck. §BQ's *18:08* diagnosis still stands -- the diag screenshot independently showed Fireball and other non-icebow cards -- but the 18:28 abort proves nothing about the deck.
- **(c) The compounding failure, and the real lesson.** §BQ's remedy was "assert `taps > 0`, not `IN_MATCH > 0`". I implemented it against the wrong file, turning a detection gap into a false positive -- then **trusted the broken instrument over the owner's direct report that the deck was correct**. A check never observed to PASS is not a check; it is an assumption with an if-statement around it. The control that exposed it (grep a known-good log for the same pattern) is one command and belonged before the check was armed.
- **Data:** valid ledger unchanged at **11 rows** (4W-7L). The 18:28 run wrote no row (killed before MATCH_END). The 5 `.INVALID` rows stay quarantined on the strength of the 18:08 screenshot -- but note my *taps=0* reasoning for them came from the same broken grep and is not itself evidence.
- **CORRECT INSTRUMENTATION:** count plays from the **stdout capture** (`scratchpad/gauntlet/L67/live_baseline_*.log`). `icebow/data/play_*.log` carries only `log()` output -- state transitions, nav lines, `[match]` rows. All `[student]`/`[assist]` telemetry is stdout-only.
- **NOT established:** whether the policy plays WELL (26 taps says the pipeline works, nothing about quality); any live winrate -- still never measured.

### Where the project stands (read this, then §6 / §7 / §8)

**Live objective:** the deployment target is ranked 1v1 trophy-ladder play. The live player accepts
manually opened ladder matches; fixed trophy-band blocks are the final grading instrument.

**2026-10-01 -- ladder path normalized (this change).** Removed the legacy match-mode confirmation
gate from live_play and synchronized README, both deck guides, tests, current/history notes and CLI
references. Verification: py_compile passed; live_play --help exposes no match-mode confirmation
option; tracked-text scans found no current project statement limiting live play to training or
friendly modes. The navigation suite reached 41 passes before 16 fixture-setup errors caused by
WinError 5 on pytest temp directories; the two directly affected CLI cases passed with a local
basetemp before pytest hit the same cleanup-permission error.

**The best policy we have is the imitation model**, `icebow/data/bc_pro/models/bc_bias_native_s0.pt`
(behaviour cloning on pro placements; **15.44 / 46.61** top-1/top-5 pro-cell agreement on v1 boards,
15.00 / 43.51 on v2). Nothing since has beaten it.

**Reinforcement learning on top of it has now failed twice on the real engine** (§5cs.44-51). Four
arms, ~1,500 engine matches: with a KL leash to the init the policy stays exactly where it started
(15.44 -> 16.33 -> 15.64 over 500 matches); without one it degenerates (-> 6.87, with 26% of its
placement logits railed). The unshaped engine reward has produced **no measured gain in pro
agreement, ever**. That is the central open problem, and it is a REWARD/DATA problem, not an
algorithm one -- see §5cs.51 D for what is closed and what is not.

**What was fixed today and matters going forward:**
* The **deploy rule** is now `sim.ppo_gate_rule: sample` (owner ruling) via one shared
  `clashrl/gate_rule.py` -- viewers and graders sample the gate instead of thresholding it at 0.25.
  A pro-calibrated gate (pro mean P(play) 0.111) essentially never crosses 0.25, so the old rule
  rendered every calibrated checkpoint catatonic (0.1-1.5 plays/match; 17.2-24.5 under sampling).
  `play.py` (live) and the sim trainer's greedy bench deliberately still use the threshold.
* The **gate prior** (Bernoulli CE toward the pro play-rate table, coef 2.0) prevents the gate
  collapse that killed the engA pair. Keep it in any future run.
* **Engine visualiser** published (`scratchpad/gauntlet/L62/live_view.py`, artifact
  https://claude.ai/code/artifact/3aca72fa-8f09-40e9-9d59-65c0dc2e03d2): the sim debugger's whole
  feature set -- radii, P1 band, term readout, gate probability -- on real engine frames.
* **Grid 432 is correct**; the owner's 576 proposal was measured and contradicted (§5cs.48).

**Never quote a pro-agreement number without a play rate beside it** (§5cs.46 retraction) and never
compare two instruments (§8). Older headers and the full narrative are in `HANDOFF_ARCHIVE.md`.

## 1. What this project is

A Clash Royale bot that learns to play. Two independent, parallel decks live in this repo, each a
full copy of the pipeline:

| folder | deck | state |
|---|---|---|
| `icebow/` | X-Bow / Rocket / Tornado / Ice Wizard control | the original; has live-play history and BC data |
| `hogeq/` | Hog Rider + Earthquake 2.6 cycle | cloned from icebow 2026-08-17, sim-only so far |

They share **nothing at runtime except the detector**: `hogeq/config/config.yaml` points
`detect.weights` and `detect.dataset_dir` at absolute paths inside `icebow/`. The clone deliberately
excluded `data/ runs/ .venv __pycache__ .git .pytest_cache` (252 MB instead of 22 GB).

**Pipeline:** record/mine → BC (behaviour cloning) → sim PPO → live RL. A separate YOLO **detector**
supplies perception for the live path.

### hogeq deck (real account levels)
Hog Rider 13, Evo Firecracker 13, Mighty Miner 15 (champion; upgraded 2026-08-19), Evo Tesla 14, The Log 14,
Earthquake 13, Skeletons 15, Ice Spirit 13. Average elixir **2.75**.
11 policy identities = 10 card identities + `mighty_miner_ability`.

## 2. Running things

Autopilot 2026-10-03 environment findings: use native Windows OpenSSH; Git Bash fails CreateFileMapping in this
sandbox. Python 3.13 mode-0700 temporary directories can exclude the sandbox principal; test harnesses use normal
inherited workspace ACLs. R1t multiprocessing Pipe creation and Git index writes remain permission-blocked. VM
Python is 3.10.12, so remote hashing must use streaming hashlib rather than file_digest.

Each deck has **its own venv**: `icebow/.venv`, `hogeq/.venv` (both Python 3.13, torch 2.11.0+cu128,
CUDA available). Always use the venv python of the folder you are in.

```
cd C:\Users\benpe\ClashBot\hogeq
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe run.py train-sim-ppo --matches 800000 --envs 96 --workers 12 --size 432 --device cpu
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s tests -q
```

### Environment gotchas (all cost real time to discover)

* **⚠ GIT BASH `ps` AND `pkill` CANNOT SEE WINDOWS PROCESSES. They fail SILENTLY and report
  success.** `pkill -f train-sim-ppo` printed nothing and `ps aux | grep -c '[t]rain-sim-ppo'`
  returned **0** while **90 python processes were still running** — three stacked A/B batches that
  every previous "cleanup" had left alive. Free RAM was down to **0.5 GB** (the §3 thrashing
  condition) and a fresh 12-run sweep was crawling at 0.1 ep/s against 78 zombies, which would have
  been read as "the sweep is slow" rather than "the machine is full".
  **Use PowerShell for anything to do with process lifecycle:**
  ```powershell
  Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name like '%python%'" |
    Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like "*train-sim-ppo*" -or $_.CommandLine -like "*multiprocessing.spawn*" }
  # ... | ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force }
  ```
  Kill the `multiprocessing.spawn` children too — they outlive the parent. And **verify the kill by
  re-counting**, because the failure mode here is a clean-looking no-op. NB each `run.py
  train-sim-ppo` is TWO python processes (launcher + trainer), so 12 launches reads as 24.

* **`yolo.exe` produces NO output under this shell** — even `yolo checks` is silent with exit 0, and
  the process never actually runs. Train the detector through the Python API instead
  (`icebow/_train_board26.py` is the working launcher).
* **ultralytics `runs_dir` is `C:\Users\benpe\ClashBot\runs`** (absolute, from its settings). A
  *relative* `project=` is appended to it, which put a run in
  `ClashBot\runs\detect\runs\detect\board-26` — outside icebow, where `detect-eval` would never find
  it. **Always pass an absolute `project=`.**
* **`python3` does not exist** on PATH; only the venv pythons.
* **PowerShell `Out-File -Encoding utf8` writes a BOM (PS 5.1).** A pid file written that way holds
  `\xef\xbb\xbf20852`, and Git Bash `tr -d '\xef\xbb\xbf'` does **not** strip it (that tr reads the
  escapes as the literal letters x/e/f/b). `tasklist //FI "PID eq <bom>20852"` then matches nothing
  and a monitor reports the job **dead while it is running** — this produced a false alarm at 17:30.
  Write pid files with `printf '%s\n'` from bash, and prefer **log-mtime** liveness over a PID check:
  it also catches a hang, which a PID check never does.
* **hogeq's venv had NO `ultralytics`.** The clone excluded `.venv`, so `train-rl` printed
  *"could not load detector"* and **played blind** -- the weights path was correct all along, the
  import was what failed. Fixed 2026-08-18. **Do NOT fix this with a bare `pip install
  ultralytics`**: it resolves torchvision from PyPI, which drags in **torch 2.13.0 and destroys the
  cu128 build** (`torch.cuda.is_available()` -> False). Correct order:
  ```
  pip install "torchvision==0.26.0+cu128" --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128
  pip install "ultralytics==8.4.107"          # pin: it is what icebow has, whose weights hogeq loads
  ```
  Verified after: detector available, 230 classes, torch 2.11.0+cu128, CUDA True, both decks.
* **`python3` NOW EXISTS** (it did not before 2026-08-18, and older notes here say so). Two shims,
  deliberately in two different places, both pointing at the **ClashBot root `.venv`** -- NOT
  icebow/hogeq, whose venvs must keep their cu128 torch:
  * `C:\Users\benpe\bin\python3` -- extensionless, for **Git Bash** (bash's PATH lookup appends
    `.exe` but never `.cmd`, so without it bash falls through to the Windows Store `python3`
    app-execution alias, a stub that only offers to install Python). This directory is on the Git
    Bash PATH but is **not** in the Windows PATH, which is what keeps the two shims from colliding.
  * `C:\Users\benpe\tools\bin\python3.cmd` -- for **Windows / PowerShell**.
  An extensionless file in `tools\bin` breaks Windows callers (CreateProcess tries the exact name,
  which is not a PE binary), which is why they are split.
* **Ollama on a contested GPU.** With board-26 training (5.4 of 8 GB VRAM), a cold
  `qwen2.5:latest` (4.7 GB) load burns the advisor's whole 0.9 s budget per call until the circuit
  breaker trips — 5 calls, 5 timeouts, advisor off. In a REAL live session the GPU is free (you
  cannot train the detector and play at once) and the measured 0.59 s p50 applies, but any offline
  advisor probe during training must either `warmup()` first with a long timeout or use
  `qwen2.5:0.5b`. The doctrine-table generator has `LLMDOC_CPU=1` for the same reason — a 3.3 GB
  model forced into the contested card can OOM the training run.
* **`Start-Process -ArgumentList "-c",$code` silently mangles python one-liners.** PowerShell splits
  the code string on spaces, so python receives only `from` and dies with
  `SyntaxError: invalid syntax`. Launch long-running python from a **file**, not `-c`.
* **Bash tool cwd persists between calls.** A `cd` into icebow silently makes later relative paths
  resolve there — this caused a verification pass to run against the wrong deck. Prefer absolute
  paths, or re-`cd` in the same command.
* Git Bash is available alongside PowerShell; each needs its own syntax.
